questions.q: Stone Town is a historic settlement in which country?
questions.e: Stone Town is on Zanzibar, part of Tanzania.

questions.q: Which coastal culture is represented by Stone Town?
questions.e: UNESCO describes it as a Swahili coastal trading town.

questions.q: Which materials are named in the construction of Stone Town buildings?
questions.e: UNESCO names coral stone and mangrove timber.

questions.q: Which set of cultural influences is reflected in Stone Town?
questions.e: UNESCO describes these influences in the town’s architecture.

questions.q: Timbuktu is in which West African country?
questions.e: Timbuktu is a historic city in Mali.

questions.q: What was Sankore in Timbuktu?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Sankore as a university and learning centre.

questions.q: Which goods were traded in Timbuktu’s historic markets?
questions.e: UNESCO notes manuscript, salt and gold trade.

questions.q: Which mosque is one of Timbuktu’s three historic great mosques?
questions.e: Sankore is one of the three mosques listed by UNESCO.

questions.q: The Old Towns of Djenné are in which country?
questions.e: Djenné is in Mali.

questions.q: Which building material is especially important in Djenné’s historic architecture?
questions.e: UNESCO highlights the use of earth in its architecture.

questions.q: Why were many traditional houses in Djenné built on raised mounds?
o: To be closer to the sea
To reduce the effect of seasonal floods
questions.e: UNESCO notes that the mounds protect houses from seasonal floods.

questions.q: Which historic trade helped Djenné grow as a market centre?
questions.e: UNESCO describes Djenné as an important link in the trans-Saharan gold trade.

questions.q: Robben Island is off the coast of which country?
questions.e: Robben Island is a South African heritage site.

questions.q: What were some historic uses of Robben Island?
questions.e: UNESCO lists these uses across different periods.

questions.q: What does Robben Island’s heritage symbolize?
o: The start of the Swahili language
questions.e: UNESCO links the site to this symbolic history.

questions.q: What type of prison building is prominent on Robben Island?
o: A maximum-security prison for political prisoners
questions.e: UNESCO identifies the maximum-security political prison.

questions.q: Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape is in which country?
questions.e: UNESCO identifies Mapungubwe as a South African site.

questions.q: Which two rivers meet at the Mapungubwe landscape?
questions.e: UNESCO locates it at the Limpopo–Shashe confluence.

questions.q: Mapungubwe is described as an early kingdom in which region?
questions.e: UNESCO calls it the first indigenous kingdom in Southern Africa.

questions.q: Which valuable resources supported Mapungubwe’s trade?
questions.e: UNESCO says its hinterland supplied gold and ivory.

questions.q: Which climate change contributed to Mapungubwe’s decline?
o: A change in monsoon winds in Asia
questions.e: UNESCO connects the kingdom’s decline to drier conditions.

questions.q: Which historic settlement is near the borders of South Africa, Zimbabwe and Botswana?
questions.e: UNESCO places Mapungubwe where those three countries meet.

questions.q: Which kind of town is Stone Town described as?
questions.e: UNESCO describes this settlement as a Swahili trading town.

questions.q: What feature is found on some Stone Town buildings?
questions.e: UNESCO describes elaborately carved doors.
